question: does the S-HL centre decorrelation at gamma_0 = 5 hold with the arrangement as the sampling unit, rather than the arm?
why: results/gamma_5_n40/ is 5 arrangements x 8 initialisations. Its 40 arms are crossed, not independent: the arm-level statistics the paper quotes (-0.0102 +/- 0.0032, 31/40, p = 6.8e-4) are an inference about new arms, while the onset is a claim about gamma_0, i.e. about new arrangements. Re-pooled by arrangement the effect is 3/5 with a 95% t interval of [-0.0368, +0.0165], which includes zero, and a sign test on 5 units has a floor of p = 0.0625 so it could not have cleared alpha = 0.05 under any outcome. n = 8 arrangements is the smallest count whose sign-test floor (0.0078) clears 0.05. See docs/14-claim-security.md section 6 and results/seed_security.json.
sampling_unit: arrangement. The 8 initialisations are averaged within each arrangement first; every statistic below is computed on the 8 arrangement means.

statistics.primary: 95% two-sided t interval on the 8 arrangement means of Delta rho_c for S-HL. Uses the magnitudes, so it is the statistic with power at n = 8.
statistics.secondary: two-sided sign test on the 8 arrangement means (distribution-free). Ceiling: 8/8 gives p = 0.0078 and clears alpha = 0.05; 7/8 gives p = 0.0703 and does not.
statistics.descriptive: per-arrangement mean and per-arrangement arm sign counts, reported in full whatever the outcome, plus the lazy-arm drift band [+0.0051, +0.0101] drawn alongside so an arrangement that merely failed to move is legible as such.

decision_rule.stands_at_arrangement_level: primary interval excludes zero AND at least 7 of 8 arrangement means are negative. Then paper/body.tex quotes the arrangement-level mean and interval, states the unit, and may keep 'the onset sits between 3 and 5'.
decision_rule.suggestive_only: at least 7 of 8 arrangement means negative BUT the primary interval includes zero. Then the paper reports the 3 -> 10 bracket, states that gamma_0 = 5 is negative in 7 of 8 arrangements with an interval that includes zero, and makes no onset-location claim at 5.
decision_rule.arrangement_dependent: fewer than 7 of 8 arrangement means negative. Then the paper reports the 3 -> 10 bracket (factor 3.33) and describes gamma_0 = 5 as arrangement-dependent, giving the per-arrangement counts.
decision_rule.no_other_reading_will_be_substituted: the arm-level p = 6.8e-4 will not be quoted as the onset evidence under any outcome, because it is an inference about a different unit.

can_show: whether the gamma_0 = 5 decorrelation generalises across manifold arrangements, at the smallest arrangement count that can clear alpha = 0.05
cannot_show: a finer onset location than the 3 / 5 / 10 sampling allows
initialisation-level variance beyond the 8 inits already in use
the arrangement standard deviation to better than about +/-27% (relative SE of an SD at n = 8 is 1/sqrt(2*7) = 0.267)
built_in_reproducibility_check: arms with stream_id 0..4 and seed 0..7 have identical specs to results/gamma_5_n40/, and every arm is a deterministic function of its spec, so the first five arrangements must reproduce that set bitwise. A mismatch means the code moved and invalidates the comparison rather than the new arms.
reporting: off-design, own directory, never pooled with the registered grid. Supersedes results/gamma_5_n40/ for the onset claim only; gamma_5_n40 remains the record of the 5-arrangement run. The registered-grid endpoints gamma_0 = 3 and 10 stay at unique n = 8 and the mixed-population sentence must continue to name both units.
